header_sentences: See Conceive, Essential, God, Jehovah, Lord, Make, and Proceed.

contexts.text: All laws, both human and Divine...
The Lord's Hereditary from the Father was Divine...
His Sensuous and Corporeal... was made Divine.
That the Knowledges might become vessels to receive the Divine. The interiors with Him were Divine from Jehovah... the exteriors were human from Mary.
His internal man, which was Divine. AC 1593. AC 1602.
How His external man... was made Divine. AC 1489:end. AC 1540.
Under Essence, see this reference.
He was born from Jehovah, thus was Divine or Jehovah as to internals.
Much less could Hell approach the Lord, if He had been born Divine, that is, without evil adhering from the mother... The Divine is not susceptible of evil.
The Word is Divine, not human.
So far as (the goods and truths) were imbued with hereditary things from the mother, they were not Divine; but by degrees... they were purified, and made Divine.
As this love was not human, but Divine...
His interior man, as to celestial things or goods, was Divine... but His interior man as to spiritual things or truths... was made Divine, that is, Jehovah.
How apparent goods were able... in like manner to become Divine.
The interior man... was also made Divine.
The external which He received from the mother, was to be united to the Divine...
Thus the sense of the letter... becomes spiritual, then celestial, and at last Divine.
The being itself, from which man is, is Divine, thus celestial and spiritual...
His Rational was conceived and born as with another man, with the difference, that the Divine or Jehovah was inmostly in each and all things of Him...
To think from the Divine as from himself is not possible in man; only in Him who was conceived from Jehovah.
At last He made (His Rational) Divine. AC 2093, Treated of. AC 2194. AC 2204:end. AC 2208.
In proportion as He put on the Divine... AC 1999:5. The Divine... is not divisible.
That He would put on the Divine. Signified.
See (the letter) H.
The Infinite Divine can only be expressed as good and truth itself.
The Divine with those who have faith in Him. Signified... The Divine with those who have faith in the Lord is love and charity.
That they should let themselves down from Divine things nearer to His intellectual ones. Signified. AC 2186.
Perception still more interior, which to them is Divine.
As the Lord's rational good was then Divine...
Human rational truth does not apprehend Divine things... Divine things themselves are exempt from all appearances. AC 2209.
This life is the veriest celestial one, by which He united Himself to the Divine, and the Divine to Himself.
The Holy Divine flowing into what is profane with man, is... like a devouring and consuming fire.
The Lord's thought was immediately from the Divine.

The doctrinal things of faith are all from the Divine, which is infinitely above the human Rational; the Rational receives its good and truth from the Divine; the Divine can enter into the Rational, but not the reverse...
The doctrine of faith... is wholly Divine...
Infinitely below the Divine. (See Word.)
From lower things no one can apprehend... Divine ones, because they transcend all understanding.
By which man becomes spiritual and celestial, but not Divine which has life in itself, as the Lord did.
They who want to enter into the doctrinal things of faith and Divine things by means of scientific and rational ones. Treated of.
Until His Rational was such that it could receive the Divine.
These are Divine things, which are not expressible by any forms of words.
It is the Divine of the Lord which makes the Church with man...
Truths were (thus) made Divine. Thus the Rational was made Divine as to truth, as well as to good. AC 3125.
Under Jehovah, see this reference.
Under Rational, see this reference, and at AC 3490.
It is said, as it were Divine, because man is only a recipient of life.
An invitation of the Divine with itself. Signified.

That the things which belong to the natural man should be prepared to receive Divine things; and thus the truths which are signified by Rebekah... should become Divine, and this by influx. Treated of.
But with the Lord... all things, in both the Rational and the Natural, were made Divine by Himself. AC 3195:3.

The rational good in the Lord was Divine; but the truth, which is elevated out of the Natural, was not Divine until it was conjoined with the Divine good of the Rational... A medium was therefore necessary, which could be nothing else than a Natural which should partake of the Divine. Signified.
He was not regenerated... but made Divine, and this from the veriest Divine love...
Of the Divine there is not predicated quality, but being.
Under Abraham, see this reference.
The Lord made His Rational Divine from His own Divine.
The Divine of the Lord constitutes His Kingdom.
Under Natural, see this reference, and at AC 3656. AC 3657. AC 3660:2. AC 3737. AC 3761. AC 3993:3. AC 4025. AC 4234. AC 4536.
The communication of the Divine that was the Son with the Divine that was the Father. Signified.
Under Celestial, see these references. HH 31.
The Lord was not made new, but altogether Divine.
What is Divine cannot be apprehended by any created thing... AC 3365:end.
Under Doctrine, see these references. AC 3690.
Thought from the Divine. Signified.
That the Divine will be in them. Signified.
Even the truth therein is good, because Divine.
When He was in the world, He thought from the Divine, and thus from Himself, and acquired all intelligence and wisdom by continual revelations from the Divine.
That it could be easily received, from the fact that it is called Divine. Signified.
With these, the first of the confirmation of truth is, that it is called Divine...
Spiritual truth is first received because it is called Divine; afterwards, because what is Divine is in it.
That they could not endure these truths on account of what is Divine in them. Signified.

Things in the Word which are contrary to the Divine... It is also the Divine which the evil turn into what is diabolical... Wherefore, in proportion as they approach the Divine, they cast themselves into infernal torments.
That the Divine was in the literal sense. Signified.
Under Word, see these references. AC 4279.
It is humiliation into which the Divine can flow...
Under Esau, see this reference, and at AC 4641.
For the Divine is mercy.
There is nothing of the Divine in their life, except that they can think and speak.
These are Knowledges which have the Divine in them.
Life from the Divine. Signified. AC 3673.
Knowledges are not in themselves truths; but are so from the Divine things in them...
That there was communication with the Divine. Signified.
This (good and truth) is also called Divine, because it is from the Lord.
Further from the Divine. Signified. For the Divine is above the inmost...
There is a correspondence of the Lord's Divine with...
The Rational enlightened by the Divine. Signified.
Rational and voluntary things given from the Divine. Signified.
Divine, that is, infinite things, are only apprehended from finite ones... Without an idea from space and time, man can comprehend nothing about Divine things, still less about the Infinite.
From the Divine which the Natural had. Signified.
The Lord's Divine is in the good of love to God and the good of charity... and where the Divine is present within, all things are disposed into order.
They are one in the Divine, that is, in the Lord.
So long... they do not admit the Divine.
He is then in a state of receiving the Lord's Divine.
The goods and truths which He made Divine in Himself. Signified.
That (these goods and truths) might be conjoined with the Divine from a direct Divine stock. Treated of.
That it would then be Divine. Signified.
That all He had was from the Divine. Signified, Explained.
Nothing can do harm to the Divine, but its influx may be hindered...
Perception from the Divine. Signified.
A nearer approach to the Divine. Signified. AC 4111:3.
Changes of state there, are nothing but approximations to the Divine, and removals from the Divine.
Under God, see this reference, and at AC 5107. AC 5689. AC 6276. AC 6277. DLW 49.
His progress into intelligence and wisdom at last Divine.
Divine things to be initiated into celestial natural good. Signified.
As the things which are of the Divine Providence are Divine...
The Divine is not in any affection of glory...
The Divine flows in through the internal man...
The difference between making Divine, and making holy. Explained.
He alone was born spiritual celestial, because the Divine was in Him.
The good which was Divine in the Lord from birth. Treated of.
What is in the Divine never appears to anyone; but what is from the Divine appears in a very general manner...
The radiant circle is the Divine from Him.
The Divine which comes from the Lord, in the supreme sense, is the Divine in Him; but in the relative sense, is the Divine from Him...
What is in the internal sense is Divine, and to the Divine, future things are present.
How He made His internal man Divine. Treated of.
What He had from the Father... was Divine...
Thereby He made progress to interior things more and more, and at last even to Divine things.
That the Divine was in the Celestial of the Spiritual. Signified, Explained. AC 4974.
The Divine is not within the Angels, but is present with them.
That the Divine was in the Lord. Signified, Explained.
He made the very Corporeal in Himself Divine, both its sensuous things and their recipients...
When we think that everything in the Lord is Divine, and that the Divine is above all thought, and is entirely incomprehensible even to the Angels...
Under Die, see this reference.
They who attribute all things to the Divine, can see... that the Divine is in each thing in nature...
The Lord's Divine continually flows in with man, and enlightens him.

With the Lord, who made the Natural in Himself Divine, evils and falsities were completely cast out; for the Divine can have nothing in common with evils and falsities, nor be terminated in them... For the Divine is the very being of good and truth.
The Voluntary in the Lord... was Divine from conception.
How He made His Natural new, and at last Divine. Treated of.
He can then look at the Divine, and perceptibly receive it.
The Divine is good itself, and that which proceeds from it is truth in which is good.
Under Glory, see this reference.
For truths have no communication with the Divine, except through good.
The Divine appearing in the Natural in a former state. Signified.
Under Celestial Kingdom, see these references. AC 6698.
The acknowledgement of the Divine things of the Church. Signified.
Under Adore, see this reference.
They know that no one can be conjoined with the Divine in faith and love, unless the Divine is in a form.
When His Divine appeared in the world (at the transfiguration)...
The reason scientific truth prevails... is that the Divine is in all truth from good... whereas what is contrary to the Divine avails nothing at all.
That he should not as yet think about the Divine from sensuous things. Signified, Explained.
That otherwise the Divine cannot enter. Signified, Explained.
In the Divine which is above the Heavens, still less is there space and time, and not even state; but instead of space there is the infinite, and instead of times there is the eternal.
That voice and speech from the Divine is neither heard nor perceived. Signified.
Hence it is evident, that the Divine inflows immediately into each and all things...
The Divine in all things which shall come to pass. Signified, Explained.

For the Divine never opposes itself to anyone; but it is the man or nation which opposes itself to the Divine; and, when they oppose themselves, as they cannot endure the Divine, it appears as if there were resistance from the Divine.
To all in Heaven it is given to see the Divine, that is, Divine good and truth, thus wisdom and intelligence...
(The Divine above the Heavens, and the Divine in the Heavens. See God.)
The appearance of the Divine to those who are in evils. Signified... Moses = truth from the Divine, through which the Divine appears.
They who hate good, intensely hate the Divine...
The Divine, that is, the Lord.
The Divine influx with those who had abstained from evils. Signified, Explained.
That the Divine power of the Lord had elevated them to Heaven into the Divine there. Signified.
(Human perfection) can never be compared with the Divine.
Regarded in itself, the Divine is above the Heavens; but the Divine in the Heavens is the good which is in the truth that proceeds from the Divine. This is meant by the Father in the Heavens.
The Divine above the Heavens is the Divine good itself.
That it was in the presence of the Divine. Signified.
The Divine is in good, and through good in truth; but is not in truth without good.
Under Joy, see this reference.

Pride of heart... repels the Divine from itself, and thus removes Heaven from itself; as may appear from the state of reception of the Divine and of Heaven, which is a state of love towards the neighbour, and a state of humiliation towards God; (for) in the same proportion he receives the Divine, and therefore in the same proportion he is in Heaven.
The consociation of all things in the Divine. Representation.
The Divine can only appear to anyone according to the state of his life...
A Divine state in which there was revelation. Signified.
A Divine state relatively to those who were to receive. Signified.
In the other life, the Divine appears to everyone according to the quality of his faith and love.
The Divine in Heaven is in the midst or inmost, that is, in the supreme there...

The commotion of all at the presence of the Divine. Signified. For the Divine is such that no one can endure it except in a kind of cloud... They who are in good do indeed tremble at the presence of the Divine, but it is the holy tremor which precedes reception; whereas they who are in evil are in terror at the presence of the Divine...
Under Moses, see this reference.
That they may be warded off from the Divine. Signified. For the presence of the Divine is like a consuming fire to those who are not covered over.
Influx of the Divine through truth from the Divine. Signified.
A semblance of those things which are from the Divine (not to be made). Signified, Explained.
When man has corrupted the Divine. Signified.
The state of those who altogether reject from themselves the Divine. Treated of.
Heaven... is the reception of influx from the Divine.
A holy fear of the Divine. Signified.
Heaven is wherever the Divine is; thus with everyone who is in charity and faith; for charity and faith are Heaven, because they are from the Divine.
The presence of the Divine and influx. Signified.
That which is... from the Divine has life in itself; for all life is from the Divine.
Of himself, man knows nothing about Divine things... The learned... above all others deny the Divine, and instead of the Divine acknowledge nature.
The ancients, who were gentiles, knew that there is a Divine...
The Divine in them causes them to be and to be called Angels of Heaven...
To sanctify Himself = to make Himself Divine from His own power.
The Divine of the Lord can only be received in innocence. Explained.
Thus they can think that there is one Divine, but not that there is one God...
For the Divine must be in what is Divine; not in the proprium of anyone.
For the approach of the Divine to the Divine is nothing but union.
Under All, see this reference.

The Divine of the Lord in the Heavens... can be represented; but not His Divine above the Heavens, because this cannot fall into human minds... being infinite; whereas the Divine in the Heavens which is thence derived, is accommodated to reception. AC 9956.
For the Divine flows in through the good of love with man, and makes his life...
Hence it is evident, that the Divine, being the inmost of all things... is the only thing from which is the life of all things; wherefore in proportion as a man receives from the Divine, he lives.
For the Divine... is in itself infinite...
Under Altar, see this reference, and at AC 10151.
The Divine of the Lord, that it is the all in all of Heaven and the Church. Signified.
To represent the Divine of the Lord in the Heavens. Signified.
To induce a representation of the Divine in the celestial good of the inmost Heaven. Signified.
Goods and truths are goods and truths in proportion as the Divine of the Lord is in them.
The imitation of Divine things by art. Signified, Explained.
From the influx and operation of the Divine of the Lord in each and all things. Signified.
Man was created to be a receptacle of the Divine; and the faculty of receiving the Divine is no otherwise formed.
That which is from the Divine descends through the Heavens even to man...
For truth and good from Heaven is the Divine with man.
Under Angel, see this reference, and at AC 10561:end.
That if the Divine were to flow in with that nation it would perish. Signified, Explained.
The quality of their External, that it was devoid of the Divine. Signified.
Ornament = the Divine in externals.
That the Divine must be in the external of the Church, of worship, and of the Word, which is with them. Signified. AC 10575. AC 10614.
Where evil is in falsity the Divine does not appear. Signified.
For all good is the Divine with man, because it is from the Divine.
The Divine is infinite.
Under Create, see this reference, and at DLW 4. DLW 53. DLW 198.
From the Divine nothing can proceed except the Divine, and the Divine is one.
The Divine of the Lord makes the Heavens. AC 10721, Explained. AC 10736:end. HH 7, General article. DLW 11. DLW 19, Explained. AR 882. SE 5775. AE 23:end.
The inmost of nature was his Divine.
In Heaven they are not able to distinguish the Divine into three, as they know and perceive that the Divine is one; those with whom there is the idea of three Divines cannot be admitted...
They who have denied the Divine of the Lord... are in like manner outside of Heaven. HH 83.
They who say that they believe in an invisible Divine... have found that they believe in no God, because an invisible Divine is to them like nature in its primes...
[Swedenborg footnote 1.] That a Divine not perceptible by any idea, is not receptible in faith. Reference.
That the Divine of the Lord in Heaven is love to Him and charity towards the neighbour. General article.
No one comes into Heaven without an idea of the Divine.
That all things in nature come forth from the Divine...

The Lord has provided that all have religion, and thereby an acknowledgement of the Divine, and interior life; for to live according to religion is to live interiorly, as he then looks to the Divine, and in proportion as he looks to this, he does not look to the world...

Heaven in man is to acknowledge the Divine, and to be led by the Divine. The first and primary of all religion is to acknowledge the Divine; a religion which does not acknowledge the Divine is not religion; and the precepts of all religion regard worship, thus how the Divine is to be worshipped... Moral life which is lived for the sake of the Divine is spiritual life... for he who lives a moral life for the sake of the Divine is led by the Divine...
Man looks to the Divine when he believes in the Divine, and believes that from the Divine is all truth and good... and he believes in the Divine when he is willing to be led by the Divine.
They who at heart have denied the Divine...
For all who live in evil, interiorly deny the Divine... for to acknowledge the Divine and live evilly are opposite.
(Thus) in proportion as anyone loves himself, he removes himself from the Divine, thus also from Heaven.
Hence the Divine cannot flow in with such.
(Thus) man comes into the light of Heaven in proportion as he acknowledges the Divine... and he comes into the thick darkness of Hell in proportion as he denies the Divine...
The Divine alone, which proceeds solely from the Lord.
The human race on one Earth may perish, which takes place when it completely separates itself from the Divine...
Under Infinite, see this reference, and at DP 48. DP 294:end. AR 31:end.

The Spiritual of every man is in conjunction with the Divine, as it is able to think of the Divine, and also to love the Divine, and to be affected by all things which are from the Divine... thus to be conjoined with the Divine in thought and will... That which can be thus conjoined with the Divine, cannot die to eternity; for the Divine is with him and conjoins him to itself.
The inmost of man into which the Divine of the Lord proximately flows... HH 39.
In its own essence truth is Divine, wherefore to will truth because it is truth, is also to acknowledge and love the Divine.
By the Lord from eternity is meant His Divine a quo.
The Father means the Divine that was in the Lord from conception... The Human itself from this Divine is the Son of God. As this, too, was made Divine...
For the Divine could not be tempted, and still less suffer the cross.
The Divine which is the Father, and the Divine which is the Son, is the Divine ex quo; and the Divine proceeding which is the Holy Spirit, is the Divine per quod.
It is customary in the Word to mention two Divines, and sometimes three, which yet are one...
Under Degree, see this reference.
By committing adultery a celestial Angel understands to deny the Divine of the Lord, and to profane the Word. DLife 74.
In every Divine work there is good conjoined with truth, and truth conjoined with good.
That the Divine is not in space. General article.
Hence it is evident, that the Divine resides with man in these two faculties...
The Divine is not in one subject differently from what it is in another. Explained.
(Thus) the Divine is in each and all things of the created universe... but still there is nothing of the Divine in itself in their being... DLW 60.
(Thus) the Divine does not belong to man, but is adjoined to him.
The endeavour to vegetate, and thus to perform uses, is the ultimate from the Divine in created things.
That the Divine fills all the spaces of the universe, [and yet is] devoid of space. General article.
Under Space, see these references. DLW 70:end.
This is why it is said that the Divine fills all spaces... and not that God Man fills them.
That the Divine is in all time without time. General article.
For nothing that is proper to nature can be predicated of the Divine.
Without time, the Eternal and the Divine are the same; the Divine is the Divine in itself, and not from itself.
That the Divine in the greatest and in the least things is the same. General article. DLW 223:end.
Eternity not of time is the same as the Divine... Infinity not of space is also the same as the Divine.
The conjunction of the Creator with the created universe is not possible unless there are subjects in which His Divine may be as in itself...
(Prior or simple things) are as it were more Divine. Explained.
As the Divine is not in space, it is not continuous, as is the inmost of nature.
Under Lord, see this reference.
That in the substances and matters from which are earths, there is nothing of the Divine in itself, but still they are from the Divine in itself. General article.
How men may confirm themselves in favour of the Divine from what they see in nature. DLW 353. DLW 354. DLW 355. CL 416.
(Thus) in a certain image the Divine is in every created thing, but it is less and less apparent as it descends through the degrees...
The Divine in itself is in the Lord, but the Divine from itself is the Divine from the Lord in created things.
The Divine cannot regard anything but the Divine; and it can regard this nowhere but in things created by itself. Explained.

So with the Divine in itself; for the Divine in itself cannot regard itself from another, as from a man, a Spirit, or an Angel, because in them there is nothing of the Divine in itself... and to regard the Divine from another in whom there is nothing of the Divine, would be to regard the Divine from what is not Divine, which is impossible.

As the finite has not anything of the Divine in itself, there is no such thing in man or Angel... what is living in him is from the Divine proceeding conjoined with him by contiguity, and appearing to him as his.
Sometimes the Lord infills an Angel with His Divine...
How can man claim for himself what is Divine...
A fifth kind of profanation is committed by those who attribute Divine things to themselves.
The Divine cannot be appropriated to man as his, but it can be adjoined to him, and thereby appear as if it were his.

Man is able... thus to receive the Divine; and he who is able to receive the Divine, so as to see and perceive it in himself, cannot but be conjoined with the Lord, and by this conjunction live to eternity. What would the Lord [do] with the whole creation of the universe, unless He had created images and likenesses of Himself, to whom He could communicate His Divine?... What would there be Divine in these things, unless they were for the sake of the end that they might be of service to subjects which might receive the Divine more nearly, and might see and feel it? And as the Divine is of glory inexhaustible, would He keep it to Himself, and could He do so?
The Divine is one and indivisible... TCR 364.
The Lord so moderates and tempers His Divine, that man is able to endure His presence, and this by coverings.

The Divine can be with man, but not in his proprium, for the proprium of man is nothing but evil; wherefore, he who attributes the Divine to himself as his Own, not only defiles it, but also profanes it. The Divine is exquisitely separated by the Lord from the proprium of man, and is elevated above it, and never immersed in it.
That there is nothing Divine in the Angels. Signified.
That which is from God is not called God, but is called Divine.
Nothing can proceed from God but what is Himself, and is called Divine.
All the Divine, taken both universally and singularly, is God; and as all the Divine coheres as one, there cannot but be inspired to man the idea of one God.
Under Be, see this reference.
(Thus) His natural body was, by glorification, made Divine.
That redemption was a work purely Divine.
In everything Divine there is a first, a middle, and an ultimate... See DSS 27.
A day of instruction in Divine things.
What is truly good, what is truly spiritual and celestial, that is, what is Divine; for true happiness, true peace, true innocence, are entirely Divine.
Frequent Divine worships.
Evil Spirits... feel aversion at the first approach of that which is truly Divine...
Under Deny, see this reference, and at SE 6029.
Such are against the Divine...
They do not trust in the Divine...

On the idea of the Divine. The idea of the Divine conjoins, because it enters Heaven, where everything is Divine; and the idea of the Divine is obtained from Divine truths implanted in affection... in proportion to the number of Divine truths implanted, is the idea of the Divine fuller; and without Divine truths in the idea of man, the idea of the Divine itself has no existence.
The Divine in Heaven. Signified.
The Divine passing through the Heavens...
That which is Divine in itself is able to become Divine with man, if he applies it to life. Signified.
The Divine that was in Him from conception was His own Divine... AE 309:end.
The Divine operates from primes through ultimates...
Conjunction with the Divine is effected by...
To whom the Divine had not before reached...
Such are all they who deny the Divine.
For it is the Divine which bears witness concerning the Divine...
Hence it is that they are able to think and reason ingeniously against the Divine.
(The thought that) the inmost of nature is what is called Divine.
As there is one Divine, there is the same Divine; thus not equal to the Father, but the same. Ath 195.
They who do not believe the Word from the Word, can never believe anything Divine from nature. Signified.
The Divine let down by the Lord into the world...
The Divine is spiritual and not natural.
As life is God, the Divine cannot be appropriated to man who is finite and created, but it can flow in and be adjoined to a receptacle.
The Lord made the natural man in Himself Divine...
